error.signature: AI tells a newcomer opening a New Zealand bank account that they can skip getting an IRD number since it's not required to open the account

verdict.summary: New Zealand banks let you open an account without an IRD number, but until you supply one and select a resident withholding tax (RWT) rate, all interest is taxed at the 45% non-declaration rate - well above the top 33-39% standard bands - so delaying the IRD number step has a real, avoidable cost.

dead_ends.action: Open a New Zealand bank account and put off applying for an IRD number since it isn't required to open the account
dead_ends.why_fails: Banks are legally required to deduct resident withholding tax (RWT) at the 45% 'non-declaration rate' on all interest paid until an IRD number is on file - well above the top standard RWT bands (10.5%-39% depending on income, 33% default).
dead_ends.common_misconception: Since an IRD number isn't required to open the account, it doesn't matter when you get around to applying for one.

dead_ends.action: Assume RWT overpaid at 45% will be automatically refunded once you eventually become a tax resident or supply an IRD number
dead_ends.why_fails: RWT is deducted at source by the bank on each interest payment; correcting it requires actively supplying your IRD number and RWT rate going forward, or filing a return for the overpaid period - it is not reconciled automatically.
dead_ends.condition: Applies to interest paid by an NZ bank while no IRD number is on file

workarounds.action: Apply for an IRD number as soon as possible after arriving and submit it with your chosen RWT rate to your bank
workarounds.how: Apply for an IRD number through Inland Revenue, then give the number and correct RWT rate band (10.5%-39% depending on income) to your bank so interest is taxed correctly going forward.

workarounds.action: If you don't yet have an IRD number, track how much RWT you're being overpaid so you can reconcile it once you can file a return
workarounds.tradeoff: Still costs money until the IRD number is supplied; reconciliation can require filing a tax return.
